analyst.summary: Power Grid is India's national power-transmission utility, rebuilding its pace of spending and asset commissioning after a flat 2020-24 stretch - it spent and commissioned more in FY26 than it originally guided, and has laid out a similar step-up plan for FY27 and FY28. Profit has not moved much yet because under its regulated-utility model, earnings only grow once new assets are formally commissioned, and that step-up is only now working through the numbers. The company has a large, multi-year pipeline of confirmed and bidding work, its collections from customers have actually improved rather than worsened, and it continues to pay a steady, well-covered dividend. The main watch item is that Power Grid is winning a smaller share of the competitively-bid transmission projects than it used to, as rivals bid more aggressively, which could mean thinner returns on future growth. At the current price the stock is not expensive relative to its own history, but it is not a bargain either - it looks like a fairly-priced, steady utility rather than a re-rating opportunity, so we rate it Hold.
